Fidelity:

- Host-exact: contracts run in the same soroban-env-host release as the network's protocol, in enforcing mode, with a module cache, metered exactly as stellar-core's host, and every auth signature is verified.
- Transaction layer: a port of stellar-core's checks (preconditions, sequence numbers, signature weights and thresholds, v1 and fee-bump envelopes, fee bid, resource fee and limits, balance above reserve, fee charged before apply, disk-read metering, rent and refund), checked against real mainnet and testnet transactions by `soroban-sim replay` (docs/replay.md).
- Not modelled: classic operations (funding is an override), ExtendFootprintTtl and RestoreFootprint operations, several transactions per ledger, per-ledger limits and surge pricing (one ledger per transaction at the base fee), and core's PRNG seed.
- A head fork reads RPC's latest ledger lazily (drift below lists any entry that changed after the fork ledger); a checkpoint fork rolls every read back to the fork ledger.
- RPC facade: simulateTransaction runs against the session's state in the ledger the next transaction applies in (stellar-rpc simulates in its latest closed ledger), with stellar-rpc's resource padding and auth modes; sendTransaction validates and applies through the same session; getTransaction's meta is rebuilt from each touched entry's before and after values, not core's exact change list.

## Safety

The session never submits anything, and rehearsal envelopes keep the real network id. Throwaway keys stand in for every real signer, so these envelopes are not valid on the real network unless a signer the network already has signed them. The facade keeps the real network passphrase, so a tool that signs with a real key makes an envelope valid on the real network; on mainnet the facade refuses such envelopes unless real signers are allowed.

No envelope was signed by a signer the base network already has.
